scope: Original RWD on optional 20-inch wheels. March 2023 test does not verify a late-2023 suspension or build-date change.
positiveThemes: Efficient electric drive, equipment and useful storage.
negativeThemes: Firm ride and road noise; many controls require the screen.

tested: 2025 Tesla Model Y RWD Launch Series
scope: Australian Juniper launch car. Equipment and warranty comments reflect May 2025, not every later Premium RWD.
positiveThemes: Improved ride comfort, cabin finish and range.

scope: Australian launch test of the original 60-kWh Extended Range. Factory tyres and warranty terms discussed are historical.
positiveThemes: Strong equipment value, cabin space and material quality.
negativeThemes: Original tyres and pedal response; early ownership-support questions.

scope: Overseas early drive in Spain before Australian launch. Reference only: Australian specification, pricing and ride require local evidence.

negativeThemes: Ride and interface reservations; Australian ownership evidence is immature.

scope: Original Air RWD, not a GT-Line or 84-kWh facelift. Historical supply and new-price comments are not current used-market evidence.

negativeThemes: Manual door handles and equipment omissions relative to GT-Line.

scope: 88.1-kWh front-drive Air. The reviewer preferred its ride to an earlier Earth test; this is not a Standard Range test.
positiveThemes: Quiet, spacious cabin and comfortable ride for family use.
negativeThemes: Base-grade equipment omissions and intrusive speed alerts.

scope: Original Australian AWD launch model. Not evidence of the later 84-kWh RWD’s range or suspension.
positiveThemes: Finish, charging capability, V2L and efficiency.

negativeThemes: High price and persistent driver-assistance alerts.

scope: Australian RWD long-term report: 2383 km over three months. Not a Long Range variant or a long-term reliability survey.
positiveThemes: Comfort, luxury equipment and charging capability.
negativeThemes: Key-fob inconvenience and steering-wheel obstruction of the touchscreen.

scope: Five-seat 20-kWh Aspire tested in July 2023; article updated for 2024 pricing. Not the updated 22.7-kWh seven-seater.

scope: Updated 22.7-kWh generation in a higher grade than Aspire. Reference only for the dashboard’s seven-seat Aspire.

negativeThemes: Price, driver monitoring and modest charging progress.

scope: 18.3-kWh FWD Essential with revised suspension, not Dynamic or Extended Range. Review body identifies the tested grade.

negativeThemes: Small boot, no spare and some sharp-bump harshness.

scope: Ti e-4ORCE AWD, not the later ST-L front-drive configuration.

negativeThemes: Fuel economy trails the strongest hybrids; engine can sound coarse.

scope: Fifth-generation GXL 2WD. Technology and new-price commentary are from 2022, before subsequent equipment updates.

negativeThemes: Dated multimedia and limited towing capability.

scope: Short grade assessment of the sixth generation, not an extended GXL ownership test. Safety-rating and price comments are dated April 2026.

negativeThemes: Older multimedia and plain cabin presentation.

scope: Facelift front-drive hybrid. Reference only for the dashboard’s AWD HEV; drivetrain, economy and pricing differ.
positiveThemes: Fuel economy, equipment and cabin presentation.

scope: Australian MY23 Techniq AWD road test. Applies directly to the added Techniq; Dynamiq equipment, range and RWD driving behaviour differ. March 2023 supply commentary is historical.
positiveThemes: Comfortable seating and quiet power delivery.
Useful interior room and quick DC charging.
negativeThemes: Ride control still trails the related EV6.
Body shape and rear packaging have compromises.

scope: Australian Sydney launch drive of Premium RWD, replacing overseas-only context. Test tyres were over-inflated; ride observations have that limitation. An informal eight-point driving remark is not treated as a formal overall score.

negativeThemes: Intrusive assistance warnings and limited regeneration adjustment.

scope: One week with a family of three in the 77.4-kWh MY23 Dynamiq. Direct RWD match; this is not a three-child-seat trial or evidence of the Techniq AWD driving behaviour. Historical new prices are not current shopping figures.
positiveThemes: Spacious cabin, useful family storage and clear parking cameras.
negativeThemes: The reviewer disliked high-speed ride behaviour and open-road composure.

scope: Australian base 84-kWh RWD on 19-inch wheels; tested car lacks the later Digital Key update. Preserve the original 4/5 score. Its March 2026 offer has expired. Use manufacturer specifications rather than the article’s conflicting dynamic comparison widgets or charger-power table.
positiveThemes: Comfortable everyday driving, practical rear space and useful driving range.
negativeThemes: High purchase price; missing heated seats and powered tailgate at this grade.

scope: One week in an Australian 64.2-kWh Air Standard Range. Direct drivetrain and grade match; no numerical overall score verified. Historical new-car price comparisons do not establish today’s used prices.
positiveThemes: Spacious, practical SUV cabin and supportive seats.
negativeThemes: The test identifies compromises in driving dynamics.

scope: Original 18.3-kWh Dynamic FWD, before later suspension revisions; directly relevant to the 2024 car, not Extended Range. The original overall rating is 4/5: the publisher displays four with an 80%-filled five-star scale.
positiveThemes: Generous passenger space, substantial equipment and comfortable touring.
